payload.summary: Supervised-Lane Sweep (SLS) claimed a supervised+plan_only row and was about to dispatch ops directly despite the row's own explicit prose gate: supervised_note/note both say 'PLAN-ONLY: do NOT dispatch -- schedule after ops confirms /pek-extract resumes.' No evidence found in notebooks/git-log that this precondition has been met. dev-team reverted the claim (row moved back in_progress -> ready[], .head reset idle) rather than spawn ops against an explicit block. Unlike BOUNDED-1 (which has a dedicated PROSE-SEQUENCING GATE for po_sequencing_* keys), SLS's promote/claim scripts (scripts/devteam-backlog-promote-supervised-lane-sweep.jq, scripts/devteam-backlog-claim-supervised-lane-sweep.jq) have no analogous check for an explicit do-not-dispatch precondition living only in note/supervised_note prose. This is a structural gap in SLS, not a one-off: any supervised+plan_only row authored with a 'wait for X before dispatch' precondition will be mechanically claimed+dispatched by SLS the same way. Suggest routing to architect for a gate design (mirroring BOUNDED-1's prose-sequencing gate, or a structured 'blocked_until' field) so future gate-clearing cycles don't silently spawn against an explicit hold.
